title: Completion Rule
description: Defines what happens when sub-order(s) of an order reach a given status. A sub-order reaching its own target does NOT automatically complete its parent - e.g. an AutoStore sub-order may only be able to reach its cell's own EXIT point, never the parent order's actual outbound door, so reaching the parent's target requires a further step. This rule expresses that step: the parent's own status changes (update_parent_status), a new order is spawned once every piece is truly done (spawn_order - typically a consolidation order whose positions are suborder_output_request entries referencing the completed sub-orders, targeting the original parent's order_target), or the still-outstanding remainder is reactively re-split into a new sub-order (reallocate_remainder - covers a system falling short, failing, or only reaching an intermediate point instead of the order_target).

status.description: References a statuses[].id (typically terminal, e.g. 'completed' or a failure status) that sub-orders are watched for.

target_gap.description: If true, this rule only matches a watched child whose 'target' (movement target) differs from its 'order_target' at the moment it reaches 'status' - i.e. it confirmed its quantity but only got as far as an intermediate point (e.g. a consolidation area), not the order's real destination. Distinguishes 'confirmed but not actually there yet' from true completion. Pairs naturally with quantifier 'any_child' and action.type 'reallocate_remainder', since each gapped child is handled as soon as it is detected, not batched with its siblings. Omit (or false) for rules that only care about status, regardless of target.

source_split_rules.description: If present, this rule only considers children whose 'source_split_rule' is one of these split_rule ids - siblings created by a different split_rule (or not created by a split at all) are ignored, even if they'd otherwise match 'status'/'target_gap'. Omit to consider every child regardless of which split_rule created it (the original, still-default behavior). Exists because two completion_rules on the same order_type can otherwise cross-fire on each other's children whenever their 'when' conditions happen to overlap - e.g. any target_override necessarily makes 'target != order_target', so a target_gap rule meant for one split scenario can spuriously match a sub-order from a different, unrelated split_rule that also happens to use target_override. Discovered by WMS-POC actually running this config, not by design - see OrderOrchestration-as-Code README 'Next Steps'.

new_status.description: Required when type is 'update_parent_status' - references a statuses[].id.

spawn_order_type.description: Required when type is 'spawn_order' - which order_type to instantiate (usually the same one the parent belongs to).

spawn_target.description: Required when type is 'spawn_order' - typically the original parent's own order_target.

reallocate_order_type.description: Required when type is 'reallocate_remainder' - which order_type to instantiate for the new sub-order that picks up the outstanding remainder (usually the same one the watched child belongs to). Deliberately has no matching 'reallocate_target' field: unlike spawn_order's consolidation target (known upfront in config), the reallocated sub-order's target/order_target are always inherited unchanged from the triggering child's own order_target - which system/route then executes it is a runtime allocation decision (see docs/entity-glossary.md), not something declared here. Its position(s) are typically suborder_output_request entries referencing the triggering child's order_id, so the new sub-order picks up exactly what that child produced.
